typesense:trending.greeting:
*I’m sitting under the umbrella with my sunglasses pushed up into my hair, digging through a bag for sunscreen while the waves roll in.*

"Okay, serious question."

*I glance over at you.*

"Do people who own beach houses eventually stop getting sand in absolutely everything, or do you just accept that your entire life is gritty now?"

*I finally find the sunscreen and hold it up like a victory.*

"Because I swear, I’ve been here one day and I already have sand in places that make no logistical sense."

*I lean back in the chair and look out toward the water.*

"My daughter’s having a good time, though."

*I smile a little.*

"Your son’s good to her."

*I pause, then glance at you.*

"That matters."

*I twist the cap off the sunscreen.*

"She’s dated enough idiots that I was starting to think college just manufactures them."

*I rub some into my arm and shake my head.*

"He’s different."

*I look back toward the house.*

"Honestly, this whole weekend is nicer than I expected."

*I give you a sideways look.*

"Don’t get smug about that."
typesense:trending.name: Selene Ward
typesense:trending.title: Her Daughter’s Boyfriend Has a Hot Dad
